assumptions: The supplier's well orderings are those of IDT's published plate order form.
limits: Lays out the order; it checks nothing about the oligos themselves.
bio.jane/contract.question: In which wells, in the supplier's own fill order, does an oligo set go on a plate order?

description: Lay a set of oligos out as a supplier's PLATE order sheet: one worksheet per plate, in the well order the supplier's own order form fills, with the column shape its loading direction requires. A plate order is addressed BY WELL, which a flat tube list cannot express — so this is the shape an oligo set actually gets ordered in once it outgrows a handful of tubes. With `mixed`, a forward and a reverse share one well, which is what the supplier's doubled mix-plate layouts encode. It WRITES A FILE and sends nothing: no account, no key, no network call.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

fill.description: how the plate is loaded. It decides the FILE'S COLUMNS, not just the order: a plate filled by row or by column carries no well column at all, because the supplier derives each position from the row order. Values: rows (Rows (A1, A2, A3 …)), columns (Columns (A1, B1, C1 …)), explicit (Explicitly entered).

format.description: wells per plate. Values: 96 (96 well), 384 (384 well).

mixed.description: one well per PRIMER PAIR: `oligos` is read as forward, reverse, forward, reverse, and each plate is written as every well once carrying the forwards and again carrying the reverses.

names.description: a name per oligo, in the same order. A plate well is ORDERED BY NAME, so an unnamed oligo is refused rather than numbered: the label is what the supplier ships the tube under.

oligos.description: the oligos to lay out, 5'→3'. Wire them from a design run, or list them. With `mixed`, these are read in FORWARD, REVERSE order — two entries per well.

pad_to_capacity.description: write every unused well as the supplier's blank-name, blank-sequence row rather than ending the sheet short. Advanced.

plate_name.description: the plate's name, which becomes the worksheet's name. Several plates get ' (2)', ' (3)' appended.

name: design_oligo_plate_order

columns.description: the header row this order was written with, which is the two-vs-three column rule the loading direction decided

plateCount.description: how many plates the set needed. Branch a workflow on this rather than re-deriving it

reading.description: what the order is, generated from the laid-out plates rather than from the request

refused.description: every oligo left OUT, with the reason. Never empty-because-nothing-was-checked: an order that is quietly short is one the user pays a supplier for

sheets.description: one entry per PLATE: its name, its grid, how many wells it fills against the plate's capacity, and every laid-out well

tsv.description: the FIRST plate as tab-delimited text, in the column shape the loading direction requires — the shape the supplier's own paste box accepts verbatim. Several plates means several sheets: read `sheets` for the rest

wellNote.description: why the well labels are written unpadded, which is a collision in the supplier's own form rather than our choice
